title: UVEITIS & CHORIORETINOPATHY MASTER CLINICAL COMPENDIUM
summary: An exhaustive guide to the management of infectious uveitis (Toxo, CMV, ARN/PORN), systemic workups (TB, Syphilis), and the spectrum of idiopathic white dot syndromes. Designed for rapid clinical reference and deep-dive residency review.

sections.title: TOXOPLASMOSIS: Indications & Management
content: **Indications for Treatment:**
• Sight treating lesion involving macula, papillomacular bundle, optic disc, or major blood vessels
• Severe vitritis
• Active ocular toxoplasmosis in the immunocompromised
**Treatment Modalities:**

1. **Triple Therapy:** Prednisolone 1mg/kg + Pyrimethamine (75-100mg for 1-2 days, then 25-50mg daily for 4 weeks) + Folinic Acid (5mg 3x/week) + Sulphadiazine (1g 4x/day for 3-4 weeks). *Sometimes Clindamycin is added.*
2. **Intravitreal Therapy:** Clindamycin + Dexamethasone 400 microgram.
3. **Azithromycin Regimen:** Azithromycin 250-500mg daily + Pyrimethamine + Folinic Acid + Prednisolone.
4. **Quadruple Therapy:** Clindamycin 300mg 4x/day added to Triple Therapy.
5. **Co-trimoxazole:** (Bactrim/Septra) is an alternative option.
6. **Anterior Uveitis:** Topical steroids and mydriatics.
7. **Pregnancy:** Spiramycin or Azithromycin with steroids.
8. **Surgical:** Vitrectomy.
9. **Recurrence Prevention:** Co-trimoxazole 3x for 12 months.

sections.title: CMV RETINITIS: HIV & Immunocompromised Protocol
content: • **Interdisciplinary Care:** Liase with infectious disease specialist.
• **HAART:** Antiretroviral therapy is the mainstay; discontinue when CD4 count >100-150 cells/µl.
• **Systemic Induction:** Valganciclovir 900mg twice daily for up to 3 weeks.
• **Systemic Maintenance:** Valganciclovir 900mg/day.
• **Intravitreal Injections (High Risk Lesions):** For lesions near macula or optic nerve: Ganciclovir (2mg), Foscarnet (1.2mg), or Cidofovir (20mg).
• **Surgical/Adjunct:** Vitrectomy + endolaser demarcation + silicone oil tamponade; Steroids.

sections.title: Stages of PORN
content: Stage 1 (Early): Multifocal homogenous yellow-white deep retinal infiltrates; macular involvement (cherry red spot).
Stage 2 (Established): Rapid spread; full thickness necrosis and perivenular translucency.
Stage 3 (Late): Retinal atrophy, optic atrophy, rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.

sections.title: Treatment of Viral Retinitis & Uveitis
content: **ARN Management:**
1. IV Acyclovir 15mg/kg for 10-14 days, followed by 800mg 5x/day for 6-12 weeks.
2. Oral Valaciclovir/Famciclovir: Induction 2g 3x/day; Maintenance 1g 3x/day.
3. Systemic Steroids: 24h after antiviral initiation (severe cases).
4. Surgery: Vitrectomy + silicone oil tamponade.
**HSV Anterior Uveitis:**
• Topical steroids 4x/day + cycloplegic.
• Oral Acyclovir 400mg 5x/day.
• Treat raised IOP as necessary.
**Recurrent VZO Uveitis:**
• Oral Acyclovir 800mg 5x/day.

sections.title: INVESTIGATION: Tuberculosis (TB)
content: • **Skin Test:** Positive Tuberculin test within 48h.
• **T-spot.TB:** Counts antimycobacterial effector T-cells (IFN-gamma); detects latent TB.
• **IGRA:** Interferon Gamma Release Assay.
• **Sputum:** Testing with PCR.
• **Imaging:** Chest X-ray, CT, PET scan.
• **Ocular Sampling:** Aqueous/Vitreous smear (Acid-fast bacilli, Ziehl-Neelsen stain) and culture (Lowenstein-Jensen medium).
• **Imaging (Ocular):** OCT (macula eval), FA (active choroiditis, ischemia, NV), FAF (lesion activity/healing staging).
• **Systemic:** HIV status MUST be determined.

sections.title: SYPHILIS: Systemic Manifestations
content: Primary Syphilis: Painless ulcer (Chancre) on genitalia/anus.
Secondary Syphilis: Maculopapular rash + systemic manifestation.
Latent Syphilis: Asymptomatic period.
Tertiary Syphilis: Cardiovascular (Aortitis), Neurosyphilis, Gummatous infiltration of bone/viscera.

sections.title: MEWDS (Multiple Evanescent White Dot Syndrome)
content: • **Demographics:** Young adult females; Acute onset; Monocular.
• **Cause:** Idiopathic; 25-50% viral prodrome/flu vaccine.
• **Symptoms:** Painless blurring, photopsia, dyschromatopsia, scotoma.
• **Signs:** Orange granular fovea (characteristic), deep grey-white patches sparing fovea, disc edema.
• **Imaging:** VF (enlarged blind spot), FA (early hyperfluorescence/late staining), FAF (hyper-AF spots), OCT (Ellipsoid zone disruption).
• **Prognosis:** Spontaneous improvement by 8-10 weeks.

sections.title: APMPPE: Placoid Pigment Epitheliopathy
content: • **Demographics:** Young/Middle age; M=F; Subacute bilateral.
• **Signs:** Large yellow-white placoid lesions; mild vitritis.
• **CNS Risk:** Cerebral vasculitis (Requires CNS imaging/LP if neuro symptoms present).
• **Imaging:** FA (Early 'Block', Late 'Stain'), ICGA (Early/Late Hypofluorescence).
• **Poor Prognosis Factors:** Age >60, Unilateral, Interval >6m between eyes, Recurrence, Choroidal vein leakage.
• **Treatment:** Steroids (macular involvement), Steroids + Ciclosporine (Cerebral vasculitis).

sections.title: Serpiginous Choroidopathy
content: • **Demographics:** Middle age; Male > Female; Bilateral asymmetrical.
• **Symptoms:** Blurring, Metamorphopsia.
• **Signs:** Active grey-white lesions; chronic progression to scalloped atrophy; macular NV.
• **Workup:** MUST test for Syphilis and TB.
• **Imaging:** FAF (Hyper-AF edges in active disease; dark/hypo-AF if inactive).
• **Treatment:** Oral/IV Steroids, Immunosuppressants, Infliximab.

sections.title: Idiopathic Multifocal Choroiditis (MFC)
content: • **Demographics:** Young-middle aged women; Bilateral/Chronic recurrent.
• **Signs:** 50-350µm ovoid lesions; 'histoplasmosis-like' pigmented borders; Vitritis common; Linear clusters/streaks.
• **Complications:** Macular CNV (25-35%), CMO, Subretinal fibrosis.
• **Imaging:** ICGA (Hypofluorescent acute lesions), OCT (Sub-RPE material), VF (Enlarged blind spot).
• **Treatment:** Systemic/Local steroids, Immunosuppressants (MMF, Tacrolimus, Cyclosporine), Anti-VEGF for CNV.

sections.title: PIC (Punctate Inner Choroidopathy)
content: • **Demographics:** Young myopic women; 80% Bilateral/Asymmetrical.
• **Signs:** Small yellow-white macular spots; **NO VITRITIS** (or very mild). Atrophic scars with little pigment.
• **Imaging:** OCT (Acute hyperreflective material), ICGA (Midphase hypo-AF; choroidal vasculitis signs).
• **Treatment:** Treat CNV (Anti-VEGF/Steroids), Systemic immunosuppression for recurrence.

sections.title: Birdshot Retinochoroidopathy
content: • **Demographics:** Middle aged women; Chronic bilateral; HLA-A29 associated.
• **Symptoms:** Nyctalopia, floaters, dyschromatopsia.
• **Signs:** Cream-colored ovoid patches (<1 DD) in post-pole/mid-periphery; Vitritis; CMO.
• **Imaging:** FA (Vascular leakage, foveal sparing CMO), ERG (Rod/Cone abnormalities over time).
• **Treatment:** Subtenon steroids (40mg Triamcinolone), Systemic steroids + Immunomodulators (MMF, Infliximab).

sections.title: AZOOR (Acute Zonal Occult Outer Retinopathy)
content: • **Demographics:** Young/Middle aged women.
• **Symptoms:** Acute onset photopsia and zone-like visual field loss.
• **Signs:** Fundus often normal initially; later RPE clumping, vessel attenuation, peripapillary atrophy.
• **Imaging:** ERG (Severely reduced light rise, delayed 30Hz flicker, Cone > Rod), OCT (Loss of outer retina zones).
• **Treatment:** No proven treatment; Favorable outcomes reported with systemic steroids.

sections.title: MASTER COMPARISON: Idiopathic White Dot Syndromes

sections.title: CLINICAL RED FLAGS: Immediate Action Required
content: NEUROSYPHILIS: Any ocular syphilis warrants consideration of neuro-involvement.
CEREBRAL VASCULITIS: APMPPE patients with headaches require immediate CNS imaging (MRI/LP).
TB-SAMPLING: Ocular TB requires Aqueous/Vitreous culture on Lowenstein-Jensen medium.
CMV CD4 COUNT: Screening every 3 months is mandatory if CD4 < 50 cells/µl.
TOXO IN PREGNANCY: Use Spiramycin or Azithromycin with steroids instead of standard triple therapy.
